newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malakoff says 86 pct power available.
newsitem.headline: Malakoff says 86 pct power available.

text.p: Malaysian power generator Malakoff Bhd said on Thursday it would make 86 percent of its installed capacity available to national power utility Tenaga Nasional BHd.
"Eighty-six percent of capacity must be made available to Tenaga under the power purchase agreement," said Ahmad Jauhari Yahya, Malakoff's managing director.

Analysts said Tenaga would probably buy the electricity from Malakoff at between 13 and 15 Malaysian cents per kilowatt hour under the agreement. The actual cost at which the electricity is bought by Tenaga would vary over the 21-year concession period, as fuel costs and other generating costs fluctuated, they said.
Ahmad Jauhari was speaking to reporters after the launch of the second block of the Segari Energy Ventures power plant in the northern port town of Lumut.
The plant is the largest combined cycle power plant in southeast Asia with an installed generating capacity of 1,303 megawatts.

Combined cycle power plants recycle the heat that would normally be lost to the atmosphere to generate additional steam and thus boost the power output combined to a standard open cycle plant, Malakoff said in a statement. ($1 = 2.51 ringgit)
